title: AWL Sublist 7
description: Las 60 palabras de la sublista 7 de la Academic Word List, con definición, traducción, ejemplo académico, colocaciones y familia léxica.

cards.definition: To change in order to suit a new situation; to change something for a new use.
cards.example: Coastal communities will need to adapt to rising sea levels.
cards.warning: No confundir con "adopt" (adoptar).

cards.definition: A fully grown person or animal; relating to grown-up people.
cards.example: Adult literacy rates have improved considerably over the past thirty years.

cards.definition: To publicly support a policy or idea; a person who does this.
cards.example: Many economists advocate a tax on sugary drinks to reduce obesity.
cards.warning: El verbo es transitivo: "advocate a policy" (sin "for" en inglés británico formal). Como sustantivo no suele ser "abogado" ("lawyer").

cards.definition: Help, especially money or food given to countries in need; to help.
cards.example: Foreign aid should focus on long-term development rather than short-term relief.

cards.definition: A way of communicating or delivering something; to direct money or energy towards a purpose.
cards.example: Profits from the lottery are channelled into community sports projects.

cards.definition: A substance made by chemistry; relating to chemistry.
cards.example: Some chemicals used in agriculture can contaminate groundwater.
cards.warning: La persona que estudia química es "chemist"; "un químico" (sustancia) es "a chemical".

cards.definition: Typical and well known; of high quality and lasting value.
cards.example: The collapse of the housing market is a classic example of a speculative bubble.
cards.warning: "Classical" se usa para música clásica y la Antigüedad; "classic" para "típico" o "de referencia".

cards.definition: Including everything or nearly everything that is relevant.
cards.example: The report provides a comprehensive analysis of energy use in public buildings.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "comprehensive" NO es "comprensivo" ("understanding").

cards.definition: To consist of or be made up of particular parts.
cards.example: The sample comprised 400 adults aged between 18 and 65.
cards.warning: Forma recomendada: "X comprises A and B" (sin "of"). "Is comprised of" se usa pero muchos lo consideran incorrecto.

cards.definition: To show or state that something is definitely true or correct.
cards.example: Later studies confirmed the link between air pollution and asthma.

cards.definition: Completely different or opposed to something.
cards.example: Contrary to popular belief, most plastic waste is not recycled.
cards.warning: "On the contrary" sirve para contradecir algo que acabas de negar; para contrastar dos ideas usa "on the other hand" o "in contrast".

cards.definition: To change something into a different form or for a different use.
cards.example: Several old factories have been converted into affordable housing.

cards.definition: Two people in a relationship; a small number; to join or combine.
cards.example: Low wages, coupled with high rents, have pushed many families into debt.
cards.warning: "Coupled with" (unido a, sumado a) es muy útil en Writing.

cards.definition: A period of ten years.
cards.example: Over the last decade, online learning has grown rapidly.

cards.definition: Clear, certain and not likely to change.
cards.example: There is no definite answer to how much screen time is safe for children.
cards.warning: No confundir con "definitive" (definitivo, final): "definitive version".

cards.definition: To say that something is not true; to refuse to give someone something.
cards.example: Few scientists now deny that human activity is warming the planet.
cards.warning: "Deny + -ing": "He denied stealing", no "denied to steal".

cards.definition: To recognise or show the difference between things.
cards.example: Consumers often find it hard to differentiate between similar brands.

cards.definition: To get rid of something you no longer want or need.
cards.example: Households must dispose of batteries at designated recycling points.
cards.warning: Siempre "dispose OF something". No significa "disponer" ("have/arrange"). "Disposable income" = renta disponible.

cards.definition: Full of energy and change; forces that produce change in a system.
cards.example: The dynamics of family life have changed as more women enter the workforce.

cards.definition: To remove or get rid of something completely.
cards.example: Vaccination programmes have almost eliminated polio worldwide.

cards.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory.
cards.example: There is little empirical evidence that violent games cause aggressive behaviour.

cards.definition: To provide the tools, skills or knowledge needed for a purpose.
cards.example: Schools should equip students with the skills needed in a digital economy.
cards.warning: "Equipment" es incontable: "equipment", no "equipments".

cards.definition: To remove or take out something, often with effort; a short passage from a text.
cards.example: Extracting oil from tar sands requires large amounts of water.

cards.definition: A collection of documents or data; to officially submit a document or complaint.
cards.example: The company filed for bankruptcy after three years of heavy losses.

cards.definition: Having a limit or end.
cards.example: Fossil fuels are a finite resource and will eventually run out.

cards.definition: The basic idea or principle on which something is based; an organisation that funds causes.
cards.example: Early childhood education lays the foundation for later academic success.

cards.definition: The world; a round model of the Earth.
cards.example: Global trade has increased the spread of invasive species across the globe.

cards.definition: A level of quality or rank; a mark for school work; to sort or mark by quality.
cards.example: Students who sleep well tend to achieve higher grades.
cards.warning: En EE. UU. "grade" también es "curso escolar" ("fifth grade"). No confundir con "degree" (título universitario, grado de temperatura).

cards.definition: To promise firmly that something will happen; a firm promise.
cards.example: A university degree no longer guarantees a well-paid job.

cards.definition: A system in which people or things are ranked one above the other.
cards.example: Flat organisations have fewer levels of hierarchy than traditional firms.

cards.definition: Exactly the same.
cards.example: Studies of identical twins help separate genetic from environmental factors.
cards.warning: Preposición: "identical TO/WITH", no "identical AS".

cards.definition: A set of beliefs, especially political ones, held by a group.
cards.example: Economic policy is often shaped more by ideology than by evidence.

cards.definition: To form an opinion or conclusion from evidence rather than from direct statements.
cards.example: From these figures, we can infer that demand for housing will continue to rise.
cards.warning: El lector "infers"; el autor "implies". No los intercambies.

cards.definition: To introduce new ideas, methods or products.
cards.example: Small firms often innovate faster than large corporations.

cards.definition: To put something into something else, or add text into a document.
cards.example: A new clause was inserted into the contract to protect workers' rights.

cards.definition: To become involved in a situation in order to change or improve it.
cards.example: Governments may need to intervene when markets fail to protect consumers.

cards.definition: To separate something or someone from others; to identify one factor among many.
cards.example: Elderly people living alone are at risk of becoming socially isolated.

cards.definition: Television, newspapers, radio and the internet considered as a whole.
cards.example: Social media has changed the way young people consume news.
cards.warning: "Media" (medios) no es "la media" aritmética ("average" / "mean").

cards.definition: A particular way or method of doing something.
cards.example: Cycling is the most energy-efficient mode of transport in cities.
cards.warning: No significa "moda" ("fashion").

cards.definition: A model or set of ideas that represents a typical way of thinking about something.
cards.example: The discovery of DNA's structure caused a paradigm shift in biology.

cards.definition: Something that exists and can be observed, especially something unusual or hard to explain.
cards.example: Urban heat islands are a well-documented phenomenon in large cities.
cards.warning: Plural irregular: one phenomenon, two phenomena. "Phenomenal" en lenguaje coloquial = "extraordinario".

cards.definition: Something considered more important than other things and dealt with first.
cards.example: Reducing child poverty should be a top priority for the government.

cards.definition: To officially forbid something by law or rule.
cards.example: Several countries prohibit the sale of single-use plastic bags.
cards.warning: "Prohibitive" (de precios) significa "desorbitado": "prohibitive costs".

cards.definition: The act of making information available to the public; a book, magazine or article.
cards.example: The publication of the report led to a public debate on food safety.

cards.definition: To repeat someone's exact words; a sentence repeated from a text; a price estimate.
cards.example: Journalists frequently quote experts without explaining their methods.

cards.definition: To let something go or escape; to make something available to the public.
cards.example: Factories release large quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

cards.definition: To change something to its opposite; to cancel a decision or trend.
cards.example: It may be impossible to reverse the damage caused to coral reefs.

cards.definition: To create the conditions or appearance of something, often for training or research.
cards.example: Computer models simulate how floods spread through urban areas.

cards.definition: Being the only one; belonging to one person or group only.
cards.example: Price is rarely the sole factor in consumers' decisions.

cards.definition: To some degree; rather, but not very.
cards.es: algo, un tanto, en cierta medida
cards.example: The results were somewhat different from what researchers had predicted.
cards.warning: Muy útil para matizar (hedging) en Writing, en lugar de "a little bit".

cards.definition: To formally give a document or proposal for consideration; to accept authority.
cards.example: All assignments must be submitted electronically before the deadline.

cards.definition: A person or thing that comes after another and takes its place.
cards.example: The new treaty was intended as a successor to the Kyoto Protocol.
cards.warning: "Succeed" tiene dos sentidos: "tener éxito" y "suceder a". "Successive" = sucesivo, "successful" = exitoso.

cards.definition: To continue to live or exist, especially after a difficult or dangerous situation.
cards.example: Many small shops will not survive competition from online retailers.
cards.warning: Transitivo: "survive the war", no "survive TO the war".

cards.definition: A long piece of academic writing; also, the main argument of an essay.
cards.example: A strong thesis statement tells the reader exactly what the essay will argue.
cards.warning: Plural irregular: theses. En EE. UU., la tesis doctoral suele llamarse "dissertation".

cards.definition: A subject that people talk or write about.
cards.example: Climate change has become a common topic in IELTS writing tasks.
cards.warning: No es "tópico" (cliché = "cliché" / "stereotype"). "Topical" = de actualidad.

cards.definition: To send or pass something, such as a signal, disease or information, from one to another.
cards.example: The virus is transmitted mainly through contaminated water.

cards.definition: Final or most important; happening at the end of a process.
cards.example: The ultimate goal of the policy is to make housing affordable for everyone.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: "ultimate" NO es "último" en el sentido de "más reciente" ("latest" / "last"). "Ultimately" = en última instancia.

cards.definition: Being the only one of its kind; very special or unusual.
cards.example: Each region faces a unique set of environmental challenges.
cards.warning: "Mi única opción" = "my only option", no "my unique option". "Unique" implica algo singular, especial.

cards.definition: Able to be seen or noticed.
cards.example: The effects of the drought were clearly visible from satellite images.

cards.definition: Done by choice, not because you must; done without payment.
cards.example: Participation in the survey was entirely voluntary and anonymous.
cards.warning: La persona es "volunteer" (sustantivo); "voluntary" es el adjetivo.
